completion_data.completion_summary: Implemented Phase 4 of 5: SKILL.md's Stage 1 binding gate no longer hard-stops on a missing/invalid link file -- it runs the read-only pick and carries the result forward as a 'Project binding' candidate surface through Stages 7-11 of the existing single AskUserQuestion approval picker (ceiling moved four -> five), reusing Stage 5's exactly-one-or-refuse discipline for the pick's zero-row and multi-row cases rather than adding a second picker. verify-touched.sh: 27 passed, 1 failed (1 expected, 0 NEW) -- the one failure is the pre-existing, already-documented deployed-.claude/-mirror drift for the sapience extension, not a regression from this edit.

memory_candidates.content: When a plan's task text names a single preview/confirm id for a picker option (e.g. '--project "<id>"') but the underlying read-only listing it is built from can return zero, one, or many rows, do not invent a new disambiguation mechanism or a second interactive prompt if the same file already has an exactly-one-or-refuse pattern for a structurally identical problem (e.g. an existing collaborator-name resolution stage). Reusing that existing discipline for the new surface's zero-row/multi-row cases keeps the file's refusal vocabulary consistent and avoids a second AskUserQuestion call that a Non-Goal may already forbid.

A cheap regression check for 'no new interactive call was added to a prose skill file': grep the whole file for the literal tool-invocation string (e.g. "AskUserQuestion") and diff the total occurrence count against the pre-edit count via `git show HEAD:<file> | grep -c ...` vs. the post-edit count. The count should be invariant across an edit that only adds content inside an existing marker-bracketed construction block, since the string's legitimate appearances are the one real call plus a fixed set of descriptive cross-references to it.

sapience_notes.subject: Reusing an existing disambiguation pattern instead of inventing one for an underspecified multi-row case
sapience_notes.value: A plan task named a single '--project "<id>"' preview for a new picker surface, but the read-only pick it depends on can return zero, one, or more than one row, and the plan did not specify how to resolve that. Rather than invent a new mechanism or add a second AskUserQuestion call (an explicit Non-Goal), the implementation reused the file's own existing exactly-one-or-refuse discipline (already used for collaborator-name resolution): exactly one row becomes the live candidate; zero or more than one row makes the surface UNAVAILABLE with a named reason and a manual command, never a silent guess.

sapience_notes.subject: verify-touched.sh's deployed-mode staleness caveat also covers prose skill files, not only scripts
sapience_notes.value: The deployed-.claude/-mirror staleness caveat recorded in Phases 1-3 of this task (verify-touched.sh running the deployed, pre-edit copy of a suite when an extension's deployed mirror is stale) was reconfirmed to apply to a prose SKILL.md edit too: the narrowed run's one expected failure (test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh) reported gate3/gate5 content-drift findings naming skills/skill-sapience/SKILL.md alongside the two already-known drifted script files for the sapience extension. The caveat is about the extension's deployed mirror as a whole, not specific to a file type.

sapience_notes.subject: A stale numeric count beside new content is worth correcting even outside the task's literally-named edit sites
sapience_notes.value: A task's own wording scoped a 'four options -> five options' rewording to two named sentences (Stage 8's ceiling, Stage 9's closing paragraph), but two further sentences in Stage 11 ('the four surfaces have four different success shapes' and 'any of the four cases above') sat directly beside the newly-added fifth bullet and would have been an immediately visible, self-contradicting inaccuracy if left unedited. Treated as a plain correctness fix within the same file edit rather than a scope expansion requiring a stop.

sapience_notes.subject: no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md's forbidden-phrase list catches ordinary behavior-change prose, not only document-draft-history narration
sapience_notes.value: Drafting Stage 1's new prose with the phrase 'this is no longer a stop' triggered the repo's no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md rule even though the sentence describes a behavior change, not the document's own draft lineage -- the rule's forbidden list includes 'no longer' literally, with no carve-out for describing a design's current behavior relative to its own prior behavior. Remedy: state the current behavior directly ('this is not a hard stop') without referencing what it used to be.
